[LTIM.2.4.3] Re-evaluation reads both clocks as sampled when the pump began
([LTIM.2.8.4]), and every series as it stood when the pump began
([LSER.8.6.1]); all `now()` reads within one activation are still atomic
([LTIM.2.1.3]).

idris.name: ltim_2_4_2__pump_timed
idris.note: The pump re-evaluates under the sample the state holds as it begins. LESS than the clause: no series.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__entry_retime_untimed
idris.note: Re-evaluation at the pump's entry with nothing to re-evaluate changes nothing.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__retime_at_entry
idris.note: THE RE-TIME AT THE PUMP'S ENTRY: every timed chain re-evaluated at the held sample over the stamps as they stand, then the cascade for the rows of the activations it ended. 'Re-evaluation reads both clocks as sampled when the pump began': the state's clock and wall sample, held since the last tick or input. LESS than the clause: a series snapshot is outside the fragment.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__tick_then_pump_is_clocked
idris.note: A TICK THEN A PUMP IS THE CLOCKED PUMP: with no rule cooled, the net a tick and the pump after it leave is Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's `iret_19_5__pump_clocked` at the tick with the tests fixed at the wall sample over the stamps, which is Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_8_4__pump_sampled` at the sample `(t, w)`. Over every program, test list, fuel, net, wall sample, stamp table and tracker table. What lets C2 (the wall moves no monotonic gate), C3a (a rising gate fires at most once) and B2 (the counts are the edges) be read on this engine's tick-then-pump cycle, with the tests this module builds in place of the gates those files take.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_3__true_at_assert_decided_at_the_pump
idris.note: Re-evaluation reads the clock as sampled when the pump began -- the tick's 3, not the assert's 0. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens
idris.note: 'Re-evaluation reads both clocks as sampled when the pump began': the `now()` gate re-evaluated at each sample reads the wall sample of that pump, and reopens when it goes back.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_3__true_at_assert_fires_once_timed
idris.note: The pump at (7, 7) re-evaluates under its own sample and finds the condition it found at the assert. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens_timed
idris.note: 'Re-evaluation reads both clocks as sampled when the pump began': the pump at (3, 1) reads the wall the step before it set, not the tick's. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_moves_a_now_gate
idris.note: 'Re-evaluation reads both clocks as sampled': a `now()` gate re-evaluated under a sample whose wall clock moved has moved with it, the monotonic clock standing still.
